thesis:
One sentence holds the whole file together: at a ~5% risk-free rate, capital stops paying for narrative and starts paying for chokepoints. Across six weeks of observations the same four physical and institutional bottlenecks recur with rising, not fading, intensity — electrons (generation, grid, fuel cycle), bits (HBM/DRAM, fab capacity, optics/fiber), trust (agent identity, containment, cybersecurity), and rails (exchanges, brokers, tokenised/24-7 settlement). The human-need translation is equally consistent: security has displaced convenience as the premium people and institutions will pay for, and time has displaced intelligence as the thing AI is actually bought for. Consumers are not buying 'AI'; they are buying reclaimed hours ('ai phone assistant', 'ai phone answering service'), guaranteed electrons (grid-outage queries, home generators), restored bodily function (robotic surgery queries +107%, GLP-1 normalisation, longevity tiers) and provable control over machines acting on their behalf.

The single most load-bearing shift is the merger of compute and power into one asset class. Google signing a 20-year nuclear PPA, Meta funding seven gas plants, Amazon's $8B Generac order, Mitsui contracting LNG explicitly for data centres, ERCOT's 2030s demand curve, Korea's reported $200bn into US nuclear/LNG/gas — this is not a theme, it is a forty-year reversal in which generation, transmission and siting regain pricing power. It is also the most reliably observed (confidence 0.75–0.95 in the source material) and the slowest to reverse, because the constraint is permitting, turbines, switchgear and skilled trades, not capital. The second-order winner is the scarce human input: electricians, HVAC, pipeline and fab labour, which sustains contractor and EPC margins for years.

The second load-bearing shift is that agentic AI manufactures a new, non-discretionary budget line. Once software acts rather than displays, somebody must own identity, delegated authority, audit trail and millisecond containment. Nvidia is building that reference architecture in the open while Washington opts for a voluntary accord, which means the private standard sets first and regulation ratifies later — a classic toll position. Cybersecurity therefore converts from defensive cost centre to metered utility on every agent action: the most durable annuity in the AI stack, and more defensible than model licences or GPU rental, whose terminal value is contestable as inference migrates to the edge and to devices.

The third is institutional: markets are being unbundled across time (24/7, weekend, tokenised), venue (TXSE at $80–100bn of listings, NSE India, Manila IPOs) and access (SEC retail private-asset proposals). Rails, venues and brokers capture the share shift; traditional asset gatherers and the domestic trading-day monopoly lose it. Underneath all three sits demography and fiscal arithmetic — Western populations shrinking around 2029, $365tn of global debt, debt service above nominal GDP growth — which guarantees elevated term premium, makes productivity-per-worker the only growth lever (automation, agents, healthspan), and permanently disadvantages any business whose moat was cheap capital: marginal housing, levered consumers, REIT roll-ups, pre-revenue AI aspirants. Housing undersupply does not resolve; it is financed away from, and the durable trades become rental, remodel and multigenerational living rather than homebuilding volume.

theme_ranking.why: The single most repeated, most observable claim in the file (confidence 0.7–0.95 across six separate days). Google's 20-year nuclear PPA, Meta's seven gas plants, Amazon's $8B generator order and ERCOT's 2030s curve are contracted cash flows, not forecasts. Electricity, not silicon, is the binding constraint, and the constraint is permit- and turbine-limited rather than capital-limited.

Every path — nuclear, gas, behind-the-meter, orbital — still requires transmission, switchgear, interconnection and skilled trades. Quanta raised its outlook; Fermi contracted turbine O&M. The scarce input is labour and equipment lead times, which sustains contractor margins for a decade regardless of which generation technology wins.

Converts from defensive cost centre to metered utility on every agent action. Tops all flow rankings, Zscaler reaffirms 19% growth into a hostile tape, Nvidia is standardising identity/containment, Interpol flags AI-accelerated attack velocity, and Washington's voluntary accord guarantees private standards set first. Most durable annuity in the AI stack.

Italy reversing a 40-year ban, Poland's mega-project, Singapore reconsidering, Korea's $200bn, record Chinese output, uranium at record highs while equities lagged. The demand source (data centres) now signs 20-year contracts. The dislocation between record fuel prices and soft equities is the kind that resolves toward the physical asset and fuel cycle.

Demand is real and self-funding at the hyperscaler level, but the financing is becoming circular (Nvidia into Anthropic, insurer-backed GPU loans, vendor-linked cloud commitments) and China TAM should be modelled toward zero. High conviction on the physical layer — memory, optics, networking — materially lower on pure compute landlords whose terminal value is contested by edge inference.

Gas is the marginal AI fuel for the next three years because it is the only firm generation that can be built on data-centre timelines. Mitsui contracting LNG for data centres, pipeline capacity races, Hormuz risk, $107 crude and a proposed diesel export ban make this a sovereign-capex line rather than a commodity cycle.

The clearest human-need signal in the dataset: people buy reclaimed time before entertainment. ~1bn monthly mobile assistant users, Copilot at 30M seats, agent-builder queries surging. The caveat is pricing model — seat-priced software gets punished (Adobe, Wix); value accrues to distribution incumbents and to the governance layer, not to standalone model vendors.

Memory is the tightest link and least exposed to a frontier-model pause because inference and edge deployment consume HBM/DRAM regardless of training cadence. Sovereignty capex (Micron Sanand, Japan, Nvidia-Australia) adds a policy-funded floor. Offset by Huawei Ascend 960 structurally capping China TAM.

Unbundling across time, venue and access is happening simultaneously and is already observable: SEC tokenised-stock approval with half of volume outside US hours, TXSE at $100bn of listings, weekend trading, retail private-market access. Rails and brokers win whether the underlying assets do or not — IBKR's 10x decade is the template.

A 107% surge in robotic-surgery queries with granular procedural intent (hysterectomy, hernia, prostate, knee) is an aging population shopping for restored function, and Medtronic raised on device demand. The dataset explicitly flags it as unpriced. Demographics make this a decade of volume, not a cycle.

Moving from budget headlines to contracted backlog (Anduril's $2.9bn Navy award), with energy and compute infrastructure now literal military targets and public attention flagged as 'not priced'. Resilience spending converts from cyclical capex to policy-mandated line item.

Supply-chain sovereignty, not tariffs, is the long war — China's rare-earth leverage, EU trade weapons, UK tungsten stockpiles, chip fabs. Multi-decade spend, but industrial flows are negative today, so the timing is poor even where the structure is sound. Raises structural cost base and keeps goods inflation stickier than 2010-19.

Shrinking Western workforces make labour substitution the only growth lever, and physical AI crossed from demo to procurement (5,000-unit Optimus order, QBit controllers, consumer humanoid queries). But the market now demands unit economics — Tesla's Semi launch failing to excite — and construction robotics remains years from affecting housing costs.

Data-centre and grid buildout collides with a contracting materials flow picture. Structurally bid, but the file itself rates it only 0.55 and notes the macro scare must pass first; it is a derivative of power-demand rather than an independent claim.

Attention at 82 with the fastest-rising consumer query set, Apple's cost-per-token argument, Corning's $3B AT&T fiber deal. Genuine structural migration of inference to devices, but hard to express cleanly in the universe and partly a bear case for other themes rather than a standalone long.

$250k/yr longevity tiers and Grail attention +180% establish a premium tier that trickles down into diagnostics and screening. Demographically inevitable, but payer pressure and deteriorating healthcare flows mean monetisation timing is uncertain and the category is crowded with unprofitable entrants.

Azure at 43% proves the monetisation layer still works, and 'cloud computing salary/certification' queries up 53% show the labour market voting for infrastructure skills. But hyperscaler equity is now judged on cash conversion, not TAM, and the capex burden caps multiple expansion.

The bifurcation is real and repeatedly observed: TJX raising guidance, Walmart raising, Nike's worst year ever, dollar-store attention steady, NH card delinquencies at Great Recession levels. Fuel and rate costs keep pushing the bottom two quintiles down-market. Well understood, so conviction is high but edge is modest.

Genuinely conflicted evidence. The fiscal/demographic case for hard assets is the strongest long-term argument in the file, but the observed behaviour is the opposite — gold at a seven-week low while 19-year-high Treasury yields absorb the capital, investors satisfying the store-of-value need with yield rather than metal. Right thesis, wrong clock while real rates rise.

Undersupply is factual and does not resolve, but it is being financed away from rather than built out of — capital rotates to data centres, builders cut price rather than volume, and the first-time-buyer cohort shrinks permanently. The durable expressions are remodel, rental and manufactured formats, not homebuilder volumes.

Resilient volumes and global rail expansion (Tencent, GCash, Kazakhstan-China QR), but the long-term structure is a threat: stablecoin rails and agent-mediated checkout attack card-network toll economics over a decade. Visa cutting $563m of headcount while reporting resilient spending is a mixed signal.

Normalised and increasingly competitive — a share war between Lilly and Novo rather than category growth. Pharmacological metabolic management is winning share from device-and-discipline models, which is a specific bear case for CGM franchises. Economics compress even as adoption rises.

Starship reaching orbit genuinely compresses the mass-to-orbit cost curve and pulls forward constellation, defence and in-space compute demand. But investable public exposure is thin, pre-profit and already narrative-priced; the orbital-compute angle is speculative on a 5-year view.

Stablecoins and tokenised equities are the real structural development — 11% of DEX volume, SEC approval, attention +53–64%. But most of the value accrues to venues and brokers (market-structure theme), not to token prices, and crypto PAC money shaping 32 House races is a political-risk signal as much as an adoption one.

Einride scaling autonomous freight and Nvidia underpinning robotaxi programmes are real, and fleet economics ('why buying trucks stops making sense', $5,851/yr ownership cost) are pushing in the right direction. But the market now demands unit economics and the capital intensity is brutal at 5% rates.

Agent-mediated intent is the largest re-plumbing of ad economics since mobile and TikTok Shop is the biggest unmonetised attention pool — but it is as likely to destroy incumbent ad economics as to extend them. Directionally important, directionally ambiguous for the incumbents in the universe.

Durable wallet reallocation — more US cards pay for streaming than cinema and concerts combined, reinforced by fuel-driven mobility costs. But it is a mature, fully-priced share shift with brutal content economics and no new constraint being relieved.

Delivery aggregation substitutes for personal trips as mobility is repriced, but the distillate squeeze taxes delivery directly and the sector carries capital intensity into a 5% rate regime. Agent-mediated commerce threatens marketplace take rates from above.

Genuinely bifurcated: Carnival's record $7.6B deposits and premium-cabin demand versus Ryanair cutting winter capacity, Southwest holding guidance only on higher fuel, Norwegian near 52-week lows. People still want the experience; the operator often cannot sell it profitably at $100+ crude. Status-dense top tier only.

beneficiary_profiles: Constraint owners of firm generation: merchant and regulated generators with data-centre load, nuclear fleets and 20-year PPA counterparties — they own the scarcest input in the AI chain and now have pricing power lost for forty years.
Picks-and-shovels for electrons: transmission and substation EPC, switchgear, turbines, generators, cooling and the skilled-trades contractors whose wage premia are the bottleneck itself.
Fuel-cycle owners: uranium and enrichment, Appalachian/Permian gas, LNG liquefaction and the pipeline capacity being explicitly contracted to serve compute.

Toll roads on agent actions: identity, delegated-authority, audit and runtime-containment vendors who get paid per action rather than per seat, and whose budget line is non-discretionary once agents act autonomously.
Bit-level chokepoints: HBM/DRAM, custom accelerators, optics and fiber — consumed by inference and edge deployment regardless of training cadence, and least exposed to a frontier-model pause.
Rails and venues, not asset gatherers: exchanges, scaled brokers, custody and settlement infrastructure that monetise the unbundling of the trading day, the venue and access to private assets.
Repair-and-stay-put beneficiaries: MRO, home improvement, build-to-rent and institutional rental operators capturing the housing budget that mortgage rates diverted away from transactions.
Function-restoration healthcare: surgical robotics, structural-heart and monitoring device annuities serving an aging cohort that actively shops for less-invasive intervention.
Sovereign-mandated capex: defence primes with contracted backlog, critical-materials processors and domestic fab/supply-chain builders funded by policy rather than by cycle.
Cash-generative, short-duration compounders with pricing power — the only valuation profile that underwrites cleanly against a permanently higher risk-free rate.
Avoid: businesses whose moat was cheap capital — marginal homebuilders, levered consumer lenders, REIT roll-ups, pre-revenue AI aspirants and pure compute landlords dependent on vendor financing.

anti_theses: 'The AI trade is a demand bubble that will pop on disappointing usage.' The evidence says the opposite: usage (~1bn monthly assistant users, 30M Copilot seats, inference at the edge) is the solid part. The fragility is in the capital structure — vendor financing, Nvidia into Anthropic, insurer-backed GPU loans, circular cloud commitments. The unwind, when it comes, will be a credit event at second-tier clouds, not a collapse in demand, and it will hurt compute landlords far more than power, memory or security.

'Nvidia's China revenue returns once policy softens.' Huawei's Ascend 960 on a Q1 2027 timetable means Chinese silicon sovereignty arrives regardless of US policy. China share of Western AI accelerator TAM should be modelled toward zero, not held as recovery optionality — a widely-held call option that is already worthless.

'Rates revert to 3% and rate-sensitives mean-revert.' $365tn of global debt, debt service above nominal GDP growth, Western populations shrinking from 2029, an administration openly framing inflation as the debt-rebalancing mechanism, and inflation methodology itself being changed. Term premium is structural. Homebuilders, REIT roll-ups and levered consumer lenders are not cheap, they are repriced.

'Gold is the obvious hedge for fiscal debasement.' The observed behaviour contradicts the narrative twice in the file: gold at a seven-week low while 19-year-high Treasury yields absorb capital, and South Korean retail already crowded into it. The store-of-value need is currently being satisfied by yield. Gold works when real rates fall, not when deficits widen.

'Housing undersupply means homebuilders are a structural long.' Undersupply is real but it is being financed away from, not built out of. Capital is visibly rotating out of housing into data centres (Kashkari), builders cut price rather than volume, the first-time-buyer cohort permanently shrinks, construction robotics is years away, and renters are organising politically. The durable trades are remodel, rental and manufactured formats.

'CGM and continuous monitoring are the default winners of metabolic health.' The 2026-09-25 observation is explicit: health behaviour is bifurcating toward pharmacological management and away from device-and-discipline models, raising the bar for CGM franchises to prove incremental value. GLP-1 normalisation is partly a substitute for, not a complement to, monitoring hardware.

'GLP-1 is still a growth theme.' It has become a share war between Lilly and Novo with rebranding and strategy 'rethinks' — competitive, price-compressing and increasingly payer-constrained. Category adoption rises while category economics deteriorate.

'Agentic AI is bullish for software broadly.' It is bullish for distribution incumbents and for the governance layer, and actively bearish for seat-priced software — Adobe's soft guidance and Wix's cut are the early tape. Enterprises will pay for measurable labour substitution and punish per-seat licensing.

'Travel and experiences are a durable consumer long.' The demand exists but the operator economics do not at $100+ crude: Ryanair cutting winter capacity, Southwest holding guidance only on higher fuel, Norwegian near 52-week lows, MGM's takeover collapsing. Only the status-dense premium tier (Carnival's loyalty cohort, premium cabins) clears.

'Stablecoins are an imminent threat to card networks.' Search interest and product formation are real, but the source itself rates revenue impact as 3-7 years out at 0.45 confidence. This is attention preceding economics by half a decade — a reason to own the issuers' rails, not to short the networks.

'Data centres will be built wherever power is cheapest.' Rising 'ai data center near me' and water-usage queries, household tariff pass-through and 88% electricity price surges make siting a local political fight. Permitting and community consent are becoming the binding constraint behind the power constraint.

'Utilities are a defensive bond proxy to avoid at 5% rates.' Flows at -87/-94 reflect exactly that framing, while Duke raised 2026 guidance twice, ERCOT's demand curve inflects into the 2030s and an advertising company signed a 20-year nuclear PPA. Generation with data-centre load is a growth asset being sold as a rate derivative.
what_would_change: Evidence that interconnection queues or turbine lead times are clearing faster than expected, or that a hyperscaler cancels or defers contracted generation — this would undercut the highest-conviction theme in the stack.

A credit event at a neoclouds or vendor-financed GPU buyer that cascades into hyperscaler capex guidance cuts; watch Nvidia's insurer-backed loan structures and any slippage in vendor-linked cloud commitments.

A statutory US federal AI safety law that mandates a specific governance standard, displacing Nvidia's private reference architecture — this would redistribute the agent-governance toll away from the incumbent stack.
